items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: And Doc, I was the happiest person in the world, because I had all my life -- see, Fletcher Henderson's band was the hottest band out at that time, see.

ctx.x: So, we said, "Okay, okay." So, we had a few jobs to play. We played the jobs and gave him the money. So, we hopped in the car. We got our bags to gether, and we hit it out for Chicago. We got in Missouri -- I forget the little town. It was only just above the Arkansas line. And we -- the driving rod broke -- the Studebaker. So, we had to wait all night and the next day -- we had to wait a day and a half to get the part. We had it put in. So, we headed out for Chicago.

And we got to Chicago. And the Chicago Defender, they gave us free tickets to go to that affair. And Doc, I was the happiest person in the world, because I had all my life -- see, Fletcher Henderson's band was the hottest band out at that time, see. His band had been hot from the early 20's on up when he made "Sugarfoot Stomp." That was when Louis Armstrong was playing with him, and he made that famous recording -- Fletcher Henderson -- the "Sugarfoot Stomp." That was the piece that introduced him to America,…
Okay. Fletcher Henderson. We all went down to the Chicago Armory. I can name every member of that band right now.
